title: Integrating plasma biochemistry and stable isotope analysis as a monitoring framework for loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) in the eastern Mediterranean: seasonal physiological variation and ecological context
content:
Abstract
Plasma biochemical analysis is a core tool for assessing the health of free-ranging sea turtles. Its interpretation, however, depends on population-specific reference intervals (RIs), which vary with physiological state, season, sex and habitat. Such intervals remain scarce for the eastern Mediterranean, despite the region supporting some of the basin’s most important loggerhead (Caretta caretta) rookeries; the only prior dataset for the Turkish coastline (n = 22) was too small for formal estimation. Using 147 loggerhead turtles from Türkiye, we (i) established the first population-level RIs for 24 plasma biochemical parameters following Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines; (ii) quantified variation between nesting females from two rookeries and overwintering (OW) individuals; (iii) examined sex- and maturity-related variation within the OW population; and (iv) integrated stable carbon (δ13C) and nitrogen (δ15N) isotope values, measured in the same blood samples, to provide ecological context. Plasma biochemistry differed strongly with physiological state: OW individuals had markedly higher urea (≈108 vs ≈28–32 mg/dl), consistent with continued protein intake during OW, whereas nesting females showed elevated lipids, calcium, phosphorus and total protein, consistent with vitellogenesis. Erythrocyte δ13C correlated with urea and lipid fractions after false-discovery-rate correction, whereas δ15N correlations did not survive correction. These isotope–biochemistry associations were driven primarily by differences between physiological-state groups rather than by individual-level relationships, indicating that habitat- and foraging-state structure is reflected in, and can help contextualize, plasma biochemical variation. Together, the RIs and paired isotope data provide a practical monitoring framework for an underrepresented loggerhead population.
